EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Q1 2024 (SE01–SE13) coincides with a major dengue epidemic in Brazil; case volumes are exceptionally high and may stress reporting systems, causing delays, retroactive revisions, and non-standard bulletin formats.
DATA LAG — SINAN data is subject to notification lag; preliminary figures published during Q1 2024 may differ substantially from consolidated figures published post-quarter.

SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY — Brazilian states (UFs) and municipalities publish independent bulletins; national SVS figures may not match the sum of state-level figures due to reporting timing differences.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources are in Brazilian Portuguese; query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — DENV-3 re-emergence was reported in Brazil in late 2023–2024; serotype data may be relevant for outbreak characterization but is not required for core case count extraction.
HOSPITALIZATION DATA — Hospitalization counts (internações) may require cross-referencing SIH-SUS data, which is published separately from SINAN case notification data and may have longer lag times.
GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE — Brazil has 26 states + 1 Federal District (DF); subnational_location should capture UF (estado) and locality should capture município where available.
CUMULATIVE vs. INCIDENT COUNTS — Distinguish between cumulative totals (acumulado) and weekly incident counts (casos na semana) in all extracted records; annotate accordingly in evidence_quote.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Dengue from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_categories.description: Official public health agencies reporting disease-specific case, death, hospitalization, outbreak, or surveillance data. Likely source needs: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (SVS), Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES), Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS), PAHO/OPAS, WHO.
International or regional health organization reports with disease-specific surveillance or situation updates.
Peer-reviewed studies containing human case series, outbreak, surveillance, or epidemiological data for the requested disease.
Structured public-health dashboards, line lists, open data portals, or surveillance datasets for requested metrics.
Reputable news reports, situation reports, or alerts that may contain early disease-specific outbreak signals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Portuguese is the primary language of Brazilian federal health publications. The Ministério da Saúde publishes weekly dengue bulletins with granular subnational data. Using Brazilian epidemiological terminology ('semana epidemiológica', 'óbitos', 'boletim epidemiológico') maximises recall of the most authoritative primary source. This replaces the upstream English-only q_exec_001/002 with a far more targeted localized query.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable Brazilian news sources (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo) and international news reports covering dengue case and death counts in Brazil during Q1 2024, particularly for states or municipalities not covered by official bulletins.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may contain early outbreak signals or subnational figures citing official sources, filling gaps in official bulletin coverage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (cumulative vs. weekly, confirmed vs. suspected aggregate), where validation and collection roles may overlap, or where subnational scope is unclear.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's dengue reporting mixes cumulative annual totals, weekly increments, and epidemiological week aggregates. Ambiguous sources must be reviewed before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: SVS/Ministério da Saúde do Brasil publishes Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos for dengue with national and state-level case, death, and hospitalization counts by epidemiological week. Primary authoritative source for Brazil.
State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (SP, MG, RJ, PR, GO, ES, DF) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports.

The SVS Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) provide structured, downloadable dengue surveillance data by state and epidemiological week, directly mappable to target fields.
PAHO/OPAS publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological alerts that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, providing independent validation against SVS figures.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and Global Health Observatory may contain Brazil dengue 2024 entries with independently reported aggregate counts for national-level validation.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak provide epidemiological context, case definitions, serotype data, and may contain extractable case counts for specific states or municipalities.

Brazilian and international news outlets (G1, Agência Brasil, Reuters, AP) covered the 2024 dengue outbreak extensively, often citing official figures for specific states and municipalities not yet in official bulletins.

surveillance_terms: sistema de informação de agravos de notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian Ministry of Health (SVS/MS) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational case, death, and hospitalization counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS (Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos with state-level and national dengue counts. These are the primary authoritative collection sources for Brazil.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (SES) and municipal health secretariat (SMS) reports for Dengue in Brazilian states with high outbreak burden (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás) during Q1 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational SES and SMS sources provide locality-level granularity not always available in national bulletins. Brazil's 2024 dengue outbreak was particularly severe in several states.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify the Painel de Arboviroses (Brasil.io or DATASUS/SVS dashboard) structured data exports for dengue cases and deaths by state and epidemiological week during SE 01–SE 13 of 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Painel de Arboviroses and SINAN dengue datasets provide machine-readable subnational surveillance data aligned to the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS situation reports and epidemiological alerts for Dengue in Brazil covering Q1 2024 for independent cross-validation of national and subnational counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include Brazil-specific data, providing an independent validation layer against SVS figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or Global Health Observatory entries for Brazil Dengue 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON entries for Brazil dengue 2024 may contain independently reported aggregate counts usable for validation without leaking into collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED or HealthMap alerts for Brazil Dengue Q1 2024 as supplementary validation signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts with cited official figures, useful for cross-checking collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Brazilian dengue case definition documents (SVS/MS) and SINAN coding guidelines to clarify distinctions between dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave, and confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil uses a specific clinical classification system for dengue. Understanding case definitions is essential for correct field mapping of cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak epidemiology, including serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), to contextualize count semantics and geographic spread.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data, validate case definitions, and provide epidemiological context for the Q1 2024 outbreak.

count_semantics_notes: Brazil uses SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) for dengue case notification; counts are typically cumulative by epidemiological week (semana epidemiológica, SE).
Brazilian dengue reports distinguish: casos prováveis (probable), casos confirmados (confirmed), and óbitos (deaths); suspected cases may be reported separately in early surveillance.
Incidence rates are typically expressed per 100,000 inhabitants by state (UF) or municipality.
Cumulative totals reset at the start of each calendar year (January, SE01); Q1 2024 data spans SE01–SE13.
Hospitalization data (internações) may be reported separately via SIH-SUS (Sistema de Informações Hospitalares) and may lag case notification data.
PAHO and WHO reports may aggregate Brazil national totals and may not reflect subnational breakdowns.
Serotype (DENV-1 through DENV-4) data may be available from LACEN (Laboratórios Centrais de Saúde Pública) reports but is not always included in routine bulletins.
Do not conflate dengue case counts with combined arboviroses counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly stated.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with combined arboviroses (arboviroses totals include Zika and Chikungunya in Brazilian reporting).
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito infestation index (LIRAa/IIP) as human case counts.
Do not conflate dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF/dengue grave) counts with total dengue case counts.
SINAN data may be updated retroactively; preliminary vs. consolidated figures must be distinguished.
Municipal-level data may be aggregated differently across state bulletins vs. national SVS bulletins.
Óbitos prováveis (probable deaths) and óbitos confirmados (confirmed deaths) are distinct categories in Brazilian reporting; do not sum without noting classification.
Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period in Brazil; emergency bulletins may use non-standard reporting formats.
News sources may cite cumulative totals from different reference dates; always anchor to the stated epidemiological week or date range.

core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.
